critic_text:
Neither hold nor withdraw on the keep-set.

The unit was opened to make `/quorum-implement` describe the stage it is, and to delete what the pipeline already did. That work is T1–T7: slug and flags, read `status.yml`, replace fetch/plan with reads, dry-run, role not product, `tasks.md` as plan, assertions. Closing AC3 to one survivor bounds T3; it does not replace T3. T3 is still the replacement (read the unit’s artifacts; `tasks.md` is the plan). The prompt file is the exception list. Treating “keep-set of one” as the task is how a reconciliation would shrink to a rewrite — so do not let T3’s wording collapse to that sentence.

Withdraw would leave the nine contradictions in place. The 190-line rewrite is the product; it was never a reason to close the unit.

The AC3 close itself is the right harder reading: one named keep, anything else unique is a finding against the unit, not a clause inside it. That is a closed set and can be asserted (prompt file named as the sole survivor of the replaced phases; those phases described as reads).

Taken resolutions that hold: AC8 covering every remaining guarantee; AC4/AC5 as mechanical document assertions; AC7 as the `AC:` suffix plus ids that exist in `requirements.md`; watched-failure evidence in the commit message; null-tracker disposition as transient, not committed, announced at the gate. Do not treat `check.py`’s transit-artefact rule as AC6’s assertion unless those two artifacts are named members of that set — use it as the reason they are not committed, and still assert what this file says on a null tracker.

Not taken, and still in the way of READY: T1 still says decide `--complexity` / `--resume` / `--include-subtasks` per flag. AC4 already decides `--complexity` (it cannot remain an auto-detect or silent re-derive). The other two are still unspecified. That is the invocation contract this unit was opened to fix (finding 2). Hold READY until T1 names keep or delete for each; do not hold because the keep-set has one item.

AC5: assert the positive text (“stops before the first write”), not only the absence of a phase number. A deleted or all-phases dry-run would pass a negative-only check.

- severity: major — T1 still defers --resume/--include-subtasks (and does not explicitly delete --complexity under AC4), so the invocation contract remains an undecided spec
- severity: minor — an AC5 assertion that only forbids a phase number can pass a dry-run that never states it stops before the first write
verdict: concerns

That reading is correct, not a rationalisation. Article 2 bans naming products the repository does not integrate with; it does not ban names in integration-specific driver files. The remaining sweep should therefore target product names leaking into tracker-agnostic layers, including this command, while allowing legitimate driver-specific references.

With the keep-set, flag decisions, assertion rule, and gate-count requirement now explicit, the prior findings are resolved. The revised scope is bounded and reviewable.

verdict: pass
